common_name: Cherry Queen Spider Flower (Deep Cherry-Red Heirloom Cleome)

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; Cherry Queen is part of the classic Queen series of spider flower and self-sows readily once established.

directions: Direct sow after the last frost in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun. Cherry Queen is the deep cherry-red to magenta-pink member of the classic Queen series of spider flower, its large, airy flower heads carrying the same long, spidery stamens as its Rose Queen and White Queen relatives but in a richer, more saturated color that reads boldly from a distance. Like other cleomes it shrugs off Gulf South summer heat that stalls out cooler-season annuals, growing vigorously through July and August and blooming continuously from the top of each elongating stem until frost. The slightly sticky, aromatic foliage is typical of the species, and established plantings self-sow freely, though volunteer seedlings may show some color drift toward pink or white over successive generations. An excellent nectar source for hummingbirds, butterflies, and sphinx moths.

common_name: Chief Mix Celosia (Large-Plumed Bedding Cockscomb Series)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost; Chief is a classic large-plumed bedding celosia series bred for uniform, sturdy, weather-resistant flower heads.

directions: Transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after all frost danger passes. Chief Mix is a long-standing large-plumed celosia series prized for producing exceptionally big, dense, flame-shaped plumes in a full range of gold, orange, red, pink, and purple on uniform, well-branched plants that hold up well to summer rain and wind. It thrives in heat and blooms steadily from early summer through frost with minimal deadheading, making it a reliable bedding and cutting plant for the hottest part of the garden. Plumes hold their vivid color extremely well when cut fresh or dried, hung upside down in a cool, dark, well-ventilated spot.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers
